 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Kelsey Mitchell was named an All-Star for a fourth straight year this past season. The Indiana Fever guard also earned All-WNBA First Team honors after a tremendous campaign in which she averaged a career-high 24.7 points on 50.9% shooting, 1.7 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.0 steals.
 Mitchell helped lead the Fever to a franchise-best 28 regular-season wins. They secured the No. 6 seed heading into the playoffs, but were eliminated by the Las Vegas Aces in the first round. The 5-foot-8 guard finished third in the MVP race.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, Mitchell wasn't the one in the spotlight on Wednesday. That honor belonged to her late father, Mark Mitchell, who was inducted into the Cincinnati Public Schools Athletic Hall of Fame as part of the Class of 2026.
 On Friday, the Fever star shared a post from Taft Athletics via her Instagram stories .
 "Coach Mitchell's impact on Taft Athletics goes far beyond wins and championships. From leading our Senators to the school's first basketball state championship in 2011 to pouring his heart into the lives of countless young men, Coach Mitchell was more than a coach. He was a mentor, a leader, and a true difference maker," an excerpt from Taft Athletics post read.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "His legacy wasn't just about building championship teams. It was about building young men."
 Mark Mitchell led Taft High School to a city championship in his first year. He would go on to win eight Cincinnati Metro Athletic Conference (CMAC) titles, nine sectional championships, four district titles and a historic state championship in 2011. He was named CMAC Coach of the Year eight times.
 After his time at Taft High School, Mark Mitchell served as an assistant coach for the Ohio State University women's team, where he coached his daughter from 2013 to 2018. After returning to high school coaching, he became Wilberforce University's men's basketball head coach in 2020.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Mark Mitchell died suddenly in March 2024. He was just 56.
 "That was my best friend, and we did everything together," Kelsey Mitchell told ESPN . "We kind of lived through each other on so many levels. He was my father, but we could talk about everything. And it sucks. Man, it sucks. It's just, you know, you wish you could go back.
 "I try to do the best job emotionally to keep myself intact, knowing how much my dad played a role in my life and being grateful for that. … It's not always easy."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kelsey Mitchell and her family celebrated Mark Mitchell's legacy during the Hall of Fame ceremony. In one photo, the Fever star held her father's plaque of recognition, proudly accepting the honor on his behalf.
